approach: A read that gives no reading now records its reader invocation as a failure with the error in `detail`, and the real driver now records why a "successful" run had no structured output. (1) In `read_once` (reading.rs:583-774), when the outcome is not Success, or the outcome is Success with `output.structured == None`, set `record.outcome` to Error (the non-success case keeps its own outcome) and `record.detail` to the error text, then rewrite the live mirror with `write_live`. Every read path goes through `read_once`: `ask`, `read_queued`, `read_unread`, `correct`, and the re-read at dispatch in run/pin.rs:167. (2) Cause: the stored error is only the fixed sentence at reading.rs:707, because `output_from_result` (claude.rs:250-275) sets `detail` only when `!ok` and drops the result's subtype, turn count and text when the CLI says success. Code rules out a budget stop (`--max-budget-usd` ends in a non-success result, claude.rs:131), a turn limit (no `--max-turns` flag in `command_line`, claude.rs:108-140, and `error_max_turns` maps to Error), a timeout or stall (those give TimedOut or Killed, claude.rs:660-666), and a denied StructuredOutput tool (policy.rs:154 allows it). What remains is a CLI result with subtype success and no `structured_output` (stream.rs:191-194), and the repository cannot say whether the model ended in prose or never called the tool. The fix at the origin is in `invoke_once` (claude.rs:651-659): when the result is ok but carries no structured output, set `detail` to `no structured output: result subtype "success"; N turns; tools used: …; result text: <first 300 characters>`. The detail is redacted by `invocation_record` (invocation.rs:155-157) and the tool list comes from `StreamState::tools_used()` (stream.rs:168, no callers today). Each later failure then names its own cause in the record. The record can show both the record and the error in the commit body. (3) A fake-reader test in run/tests.rs, a stand-in-CLI test in claude.rs, and a CHANGELOG entry that states the cause honestly: stored errors showed one sentence, the checked causes are ruled out, and the remaining one is unproven until the next record carries the new detail.

decisions.choice: Make the change in `read_once` (reading.rs), not in `first_reading`, `read_unread` or the commit-body code.
decisions.reason: `read_once` is where the record and the error are both in hand, and `read_for` (reading.rs:524) is the only caller of it, so the fix covers all five read entry points. Exits of the changed stage: (a) driver error (`invoke_and_record` returns Err): bail at reading.rs:692, no invocation exists, unchanged. (b) outcome not Success: reading.rs:695-701 returns Failed(why) with the record's outcome kept and detail now always set, `read_for` returns vec![first] (542), `first_reading` commits it at 1233-1250 with subject '(the reader failed)', and the drain reads that state next via `read_unread` (run/mod.rs:483). (c) Success with no structured output (the new case): the record becomes Error with the error in detail, then the same path as (b). (d) reading refused by a rule (reading.rs:760-771): record stays Success with `reading_attempt` set, `read_for` re-reads once (541-577), unchanged; a refused reading is output the reader did give. (e) reading built (754-758): unchanged. (f) interrupt or kill: `interrupted_record` (invocation.rs:269-335) records Killed, and a stopped kill switch is the DriverError of (a); neither is touched. Hold: a budget hold happens before the reader runs, in `check_budget`/`preflight` (reading.rs:598, 1215), unchanged.

rejected.option: Set the outcome in `first_reading` and `read_unread` only
rejected.why: Those two functions only commit; they would miss `correct` (reading.rs:1431) and run/pin.rs:167, and the record would be edited after the live mirror was written.

rejected.option: Add a new record type or file for failed reads
rejected.why: Out of scope, and the invocation record's `outcome` and `detail` fields already carry a failure and its reason (records.rs:767-768).

decisions.choice: Reuse `InvocationOutcome::Error` and `Invocation.detail`. The outcome enum (records.rs:134-143) has Success, Error, Killed, TimedOut and Missing; `output_from_result` already uses Error for a CLI result that reports an error (claude.rs:252-256), with the reason in `detail`.
decisions.reason: The field's existing use is an invocation that ran and failed, with the reason as detail (AgentOutput doc, lib.rs:127-129). A reader run that ended with no reading fits that meaning, so no new field and no athena.toml key is needed.

rejected.option: Add a new `InvocationOutcome` variant such as NoOutput
rejected.why: It would change the records schema and every match on the enum (status.rs:958, display.rs:498, 1882), for no information Error with a detail does not give.

decisions.choice: Name the cause by recording what the CLI said, in `invoke_once` of claude.rs (a new helper beside `output_from_result`), and leave `output_from_result` and its signature alone.
decisions.reason: The tool names live in `StreamState` (stream.rs:54, 168) and not in the result event, so only `invoke_once` (claude.rs:593-659) has both. `output_from_result` is called from tests (invocation.rs:411, disk.rs:584, tests/retry.rs:1306) and keeps its behavior. Every other consumer reads `detail` only after `outcome != Success` (producer.rs:407-420, planning.rs:462 and 666, verification.rs:277, steward.rs:1306, pin.rs:476, auditor.rs:397, audience.rs:285, hestia.rs:2886, introspect.rs:1681), and `api_error_status` and `usage_limit_hit` (claude.rs:300, 334) return None for text that starts with 'no structured output'.

rejected.option: Parse `result.text` as JSON or take the last StructuredOutput tool_use input in stream.rs as a fallback reading
rejected.why: It guesses a cause the repository cannot show, and it would change what every role accepts. The new detail shows which case it is; a fallback can follow once a record names it.

rejected.option: Change the reader schema, brief (briefs.rs) or budget now
rejected.why: Nothing in the code shows the schema, brief or budget is at fault: reader_usd and the 86400 s timeout (config.rs:1028) end in non-success outcomes, not in a success with no output. A change would be a guess and would alter the reader prompt for every job.

rejected.option: Re-read automatically in `read_for` when no structured output comes back
rejected.why: It spends another reader call per failure ($0.12-0.17 each) before the cause is known; the drain already reads an unread job again once (drain.rs:4219 test).

files.purpose: In `read_once` (695-710), set `record.outcome` to Error (non-success outcomes keep theirs) and `record.detail` to the error text before returning Failed, rewrite the live mirror with `write_live`, and keep the returned `ReadError::Failed` text containing 'the reader returned no structured reading' (the drain tests match on it).

In `invoke_once` (651-659), add a helper that sets `detail` on an ok result with no structured output (subtype, turns, `state.tools_used()`, first 300 characters of the result text); add a stand-in MODE `no_structured` and a test whose name contains `no_structured`.
Add the fake-reader test `no_structured_reading_is_recorded_as_a_failed_invocation_with_the_error` (name contains `no_structured`) next to the tests that use `athena_with` and `Records::load`.

Add one bullet under `## [Unreleased]` / `### Fixed`: failed reads are recorded as failed invocations with the error in detail, the cause section (stored error, checked and ruled out, remaining cause) and the fix, with the test commands.

steps: Read crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs 683-711 and crates/athena-agent/src/claude.rs 536-686 again before editing.

In reading.rs `read_once`: after `invoke_and_record`, make a small helper `fail_record(&self, record: &mut Invocation, why: &str) -> Result<()>` that sets `record.outcome` to `InvocationOutcome::Error` only when it is Success, sets `record.detail = Some(why)`, and calls `self.state.write_live(job, &any.canonical_path(), any.to_json().as_bytes())` with `AnyRecord::Invocation(Box::new(record.clone()))` (as invocation.rs:259-261 does). Use it in the non-Success branch with `why` = the record's detail or 'the reader did not complete', and in the `structured == None` branch with 'the reader returned no structured reading', followed by ': ' and the driver's detail when the record already has one. Return `ReadError::Failed` with the same text.

In claude.rs add `fn note_missing_structured(output: &mut AgentOutput, result: &ResultEvent, tools: &[String])`, which for `output.outcome == Success && output.structured.is_none()` sets `output.detail` to `no structured output: result subtype "<subtype>"; <turns> turns; tools used: <names or none>; result text: <first 300 characters>`. Call it in `invoke_once` on the `(Some(result), _)` arm with `state.tools_used()`. Leave `output_from_result` unchanged.

Add the stand-in MODE `no_structured` to the `STAND_IN` script at claude.rs:879 (a success result with `is_error:false`, no structured_output and a `result` text) and a test `a_result_with_no_structured_output_says_so_in_the_detail_no_structured` that drives `driver.invoke` and asserts the outcome Success, `structured == None`, and the detail text. Run `cargo test -p athena-agent no_structured`.

Add the test `no_structured_reading_is_recorded_as_a_failed_invocation_with_the_error` to crates/athena-core/src/run/tests.rs, with a script wrapper that sets `turn.structured = None` for `Role::Reader`, a call to `athena.ask`, and assertions on the stored Reader invocation's outcome and detail after `Records::load`; also assert the same after `athena.read_unread` for a second read. Add the CHANGELOG bullet under `### Fixed` in `## [Unreleased]`: what changed (failed reads recorded as Error with the error in detail; the driver records why a success had no structured output), the stored error (one fixed sentence, reading.rs:707), what was checked and ruled out with file:line (budget, turn limit, timeout, stall, tool denial), that the cause between the model ending in prose and a CLI result without the field is not shown by the stored errors, the limits (cause not proven, effect on the failure rate not measured), and the tests by command.

Run `cargo fmt --all`, then `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked`; fix any existing test that expected `detail == None` on a success with no structured output only if it is a claude.rs stand-in test of the real driver.

risks.risk: The cause cannot be found from the code. The reader keeps returning no structured reading after this change; the change records why but does not by itself stop the failure.
risks.mitigation: The cause is not proven. The CHANGELOG entry says so and lists what was checked, the fix records the cause for the next failure, and the open question asks the host for the old runs' data. A follow-up fix (a fallback or a brief change) can then name its evidence.

risks.risk: A claude.rs stand-in test, or a test elsewhere, asserts `detail` is None on a Success with no structured output.
risks.mitigation: The real-driver path is the only one changed. The producer runs `cargo test --locked` and `cargo test -p athena-agent`; if a stand-in test asserts `detail == None` on a success without a structured output, the new detail is the intended change and the test is updated in the same step.

risks.risk: The result text quotes the request or a secret and lands in a record.
risks.mitigation: The text goes through `invocation_record`'s `redact_all` (invocation.rs:155-157) before it is stored, is cut to 300 characters, and `failed_reading_body` redacts again and truncates the commit body (reading.rs:1485-1495).

risks.risk: The live mirror written by `invoke_and_record` (invocation.rs:259-261) still holds the old Success record if the producer does not rewrite it.
risks.mitigation: The mirror is rewritten with the changed record in the same function (`write_live`), so `athena close` and the committed file agree.

risks.risk: A measure from records that counts reader invocations by outcome changes.
risks.mitigation: Only the reader's record changes; a count of failed reads now exists as outcome Error with the reader's role, and the scoring code that reads readers (score/lib.rs:456-471) uses role and model, not outcome.
